newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares keep up advance on new record levels.
newsitem.headline: German shares keep up advance on new record levels.

text.p: German shares kept up their advance on new record levels in pre-bourse dealings on Friday, posting gains despite overnight Wall Street losses.
The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings, was up 7.02 points at 3,827.18 points as a firmer dollar and gains in German debt markets also gave the market a positive tone.
"Dealings are relatively quiet this morning but there's no sign that the market is going to break down anytime soon," said one Frankfurt trader. "The uptrend appears to still be intact."
A lack of fresh corporate news kept dealings focused on technical market factors, which traders said pointed to gains.

They specifically said the market was keen on automobile shares as Volkswagen AG and BMW AG both were among top percentage gainers. VW was up 13 marks at 1,792 marks and BMW was up 16.60 marks at 1,445 marks.
"A lot of the banks are telling clients to take another look at the carmakers, that they have not kept up the other sectors in this rally," said one trader.

Among other shares, airline Lufthansa AG was up 25 pfennigs at 34.70 marks after saying on Thursday at its annual general meeting that it expected first-half profit to be higher than in the 1995 and 1996 periods.
Afternoon dealings are expected to focus on Wall Street and the release at 1230 GMT of final U.S. first quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data.
